D001-D011_h001.question:
Well, I guess I'm here because my husband finally put his foot down. He says I can't keep living like this, and honestly, neither can he. It’s hard to even explain, but it feels like my brain is always buzzing. I can’t seem to keep things in order – not my desk at work, not the house, not even my thoughts. I'll be trying to focus on a new task, like a new spreadsheet, and then my mind just drifts off to some new idea, or I get distracted by the chatter in the office. It's like any little thing can pull my attention away, even just a random thought popping into my head.

And I’m always moving. My colleagues joke I have ants in my pants. I fidget, I tap my foot, I just can't sit still for long. And I talk, a lot. Sometimes I blurt things out without thinking, which has led to some awkward moments. My husband says it’s like I'm “driven by a motor” sometimes. This isn’t new, either. My mom always told me I was a handful as a kid, always running around and interrupting. The hardest part is, these distractions aren't because I'm worried about anything. It's more like everything *else* is just so much more interesting than what I should be doing. Sometimes I get really anxious *because* I can’t focus, but it’s not really the *cause* of the inattention itself.
D001-D011_h001.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
